subject: Support Accelerator: pricing structure & SLA bundling options
messages:
From: Aisha Gomez <aisha.gomez@heliotech.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Connell <liam.oconnell@heliotech.com>
Date: 2026-10-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — SLA lanes and preferred pricing

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. HelioTech is evaluating Redwood for a customer-facing inference workload and we need a clear breakdown of support tiers and how pricing changes with uptime/response commitments. Specifically, procurement wants:

- A compact SKU for predictable monthly spend for dev/staging vs. prod (50–200k tokens/day)
- Uptime tiers (99.5 / 99.9 / 99.95) with corresponding crediting approach
- Response windows for P1/P2 and escalation coverage during weekends
- Any volume-based discounts or commit thresholds that change unit rates

Can you send a short, itemized packet we can use to share with procurement? We need it by Tue 10/20 to align with our vendor review.

Best,
Aisha
Head of Platform Engineering
HelioTech

[Attachment: RFP_sample_requirements.txt (txt)]

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Gomez <aisha.gomez@heliotech.com>, Procurements <procurements@heliotech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Support Accelerator: pricing structure & SLA bundling options

Hi Aisha —

Appreciate the clear ask. I put together three concise options below to share with procurement; attached is a 1-page summary (SLA_Pack_Pricing_v3.pdf) and a draft mutual action plan (MAA-HelioTech-2026-draft.docx). High level: we keep the unit token price separate from support SKU pricing so you can pick the support coverage that matches your operational risk.

Option A — Standard Support (no retainer)- Uptime: 99.5%- P1 response: 4 business hours- P2 response: 1 business day- Escalation: online ticketing + email; on-call only for critical incidents (ad hoc)- Price: Support SKU $0/month (included), per-token pricing unchanged- Credits: SLA credits capped at 5% of monthly invoice

Option B — Accelerated Response (recommended for production)- Uptime: 99.9%- P1 response: 1 hour (24/7)- P2 response: 4 business hours- Escalation: Dedicated on-call triage + named technical lead during outbreaks- Price: Support SKU $8,000/month retainer (covers up to 2 named services)- Credits: SLA credits escalated to 7.5% for measured downtime beyond threshold- Volume concession: 10% off support SKU with annual commit >= $250k

Option C — Assurance Plus (enterprise guarantee)- Uptime: 99.95%- P1 response: 30 minutes (24/7)- P2 response: 1 hour- Escalation: Priority routing, quarterly architecture reviews, runbook maintenance- Price: Support SKU $22,000/month retainer- Credits: 12.5% SLA credit banding, faster remediation playbooks- Volume concession: support SKU reduced by 20% on a 12-month $600k+ commit

Notes and tradeoffs:
- Batching/caching recommendations can materially reduce cost — we can run a quick usage analysis to estimate token reduction.
- Credits are invoiced as account-level credits applied to the following month; we can structure partial refunds for enterprise deals.
- All retainer SKUs include a 60-day transition period where on-call coverage is ramped.

Next steps: if procurement likes Option B or C, Marissa can provide formal commercial language and an initial price anchor for negotiation. If you want, we can also prepare a vendor-side SOW that ties the retainer to SLO metrics.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: SLA_Pack_Pricing_v3.pdf (pdf)]

On Mon, Oct 18, 2026 at 11:05 AM kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Aisha —
> 
> Appreciate the clear ask. I put together three concise options below to share with procurement; attached is a 1-page summary...

Thanks — this is very helpful. A few clarifying Qs from procurement:

1) For Option B, is the $8k retainer a flat fee regardless of request volume, or do incidents above a threshold bill against time & materials?
2) How are multi-region failovers handled if we use Dedicated capacity in two regions? Would the retainer cover cross-region failover coordination?
3) Can credits be capped as a percentage of the retainer instead of invoice value? Procurement prefers fixed upper-bounds to model worst-case liability.

Ideally we want a one-sheet that procurement can sign off on with explicit answers to the above. Can Marissa or Kimberly send a short addendum addressing these points?

—Liam
Senior Procurement Manager
HelioTech

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T15:38:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: HelioTech procurement Qs — requested clarifications and approval path

Kim / Jonas — forwarding HelioTech's procurement questions. My suggested responses below; flagging for quick approval so we can send a single-page addendum by EOD for their Tue deadline.

Suggested answers to procurement Qs:
1) Retainer billing model: Option B retainer is a flat monthly fee that covers on-call triage and up to 40 engineering-hours/month of incident response. Additional hours billed at $250/hr (time & materials) — we can convert to a blended incident overage rate at >100 incidents/quarter.
2) Multi-region failover: retainer includes cross-region coordination for failovers as part of the named-technical-lead service during the retainer window. If dedicated clusters are deployed in region pairs, runbook execution is included; travel or on-prem presence is out of scope.
3) Credits cap: we can cap credits to a percentage of the retainer for commercial simplicity (suggest capped at 150% of monthly retainer). If they prefer cap on invoice value, we can provide both options in the addendum.

Approval ask: Jonas — OK to present the above concessions? If you approve, I'll draft the one-page addendum and loop in legal for the MAA edits.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: MAA-HelioTech-2026-draft.docx (docx)]
